state_matches.reason: Both represent the initial state upon TCP connection before greeting is processed.

Service_Available after receiving 200 could map to TransitMode (server in transit/general mode before MODE READER), but it's a weak match since TransitMode is not directly reached from Established via 200 in the candidate.
Both represent the terminal closed connection state.
Both represent a state where posting is allowed. In GT it's reached after MODE READER; in candidate it's reached directly from greeting 200.
Both represent a state where posting is prohibited, reached after 201 greeting.
Both represent the state where a newsgroup has been selected.
No candidate state corresponds to a state after fetching an article but before reading headers/body.
No candidate state corresponds to reading article headers.
No candidate state corresponds to reading article body.
Both represent the state where an article is being submitted/posted, awaiting the result (240 or 441).

transition_matches.reason: Both transition from initial state on receiving 200 greeting. Destination states differ in naming but both represent an active service state. However GT goes to Service_Available (pre-MODE READER) while candidate goes directly to PostingAllowed.
Both transition from initial state on receiving 201 to a posting-prohibited state.
Both transition from initial state on 502 to closed.
Both transition from initial state on 400 to closed.

candidate.action: send 200 response; switch capabilities to reader mode

transition_matches.reason: Both involve MODE READER from a general service state to a reader/posting-allowed state. But the state mappings are weak (Service_Available~TransitMode, Posting_Allowed~ReaderModePostAllowed).
No candidate transition from PostingProhibited on MODE READER to a posting-allowed state.
Both select a newsgroup and transition to GroupSelected. Source states differ (PostingAllowed vs NoGroupSelected) but the protocol action is the same.
No candidate transition for ARTICLE command from GroupSelected to an Article_Selected state.
Both initiate POST and transition to an article-input/posting state. Source states differ (GroupSelected vs PostingAllowed) but the protocol semantics match.
No candidate state or transition for HEAD command.
No candidate state or transition for BODY command.
Both represent successful article posting (240). Source states match (Posting_Article~ArticleInput). Destination differs (GroupSelected vs PostingAllowed) but semantically returns to active state.
Both represent failed article posting (441). Source states match. Destination differs but semantically returns to active state.
No direct QUIT transition from GroupSelected in candidate. The candidate has QUIT from CommandExchange and PostingAllowed/PostingProhibited but not from GroupSelected.
